metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully attached aws-bill.pdf to the 'New-month AWS Bill' compose window in 5 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Thunderbird compose window, attach files, interact with Bcc address fields.
metadata.explanation: Chains the proven attach goal with adding a BCC address. Getter reads the accessibility tree of the open compose window to check 'aws-bill.pdf' in the attachment area and 'finance@outlook.com' in the Bcc field. Initial state has no BCC and no attachment, so evaluator will not pass spuriously. Partial credit: 0.5 per sub-goal. [Fixed: evaluator.func updated to include 'check_' prefix to match actual metric function name check_thunderbird_compose_bcc_attachment__d67afa1e0d57a9bbcae95982d894cc83]

scoring_breakdown.has_attachment: 0.5 - aws-bill.pdf visible in compose window attachment area

fix_history: Fix 1: Changed evaluator.func from 'thunderbird_compose_bcc_attachment__d67afa1e0d57a9bbcae95982d894cc83' to 'check_thunderbird_compose_bcc_attachment__d67afa1e0d57a9bbcae95982d894cc83' to match the actual metric function name in metrics/thunderbird_compose.py

llm_judge_reasons: Attachment check is semantically valid: getter searches for 'aws-bill.pdf' in the accessibility tree, which Thunderbird populates with attachment filenames when a file is attached to the compose window.

BCC check has a semantic gap: getter searches for 'finance@outlook.com' anywhere in the full accessibility tree string, not specifically within the BCC field. This could produce false positives if the agent places the email in the TO or CC field instead of BCC.
Compose window 'keep open' requirement is implicitly verified: if the compose window is closed, neither the attachment text nor the BCC address would appear in the accessibility tree.
Metric logic is logically sound: 0.5 partial credit per sub-goal (attachment + BCC) with boolean truthiness checks is appropriate for a 2-requirement task.
Metric function ignores the 'expected' parameter and encodes the pass criteria directly in logic, which is acceptable since the check is binary (present or not present).

Rule validation failure appears stale: the stored error references the old function name without 'check_' prefix, but the current evaluator.func correctly has the 'check_' prefix matching the metric file.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Improve BCC field specificity: instead of a full-tree substring search, parse the accessibility tree to locate the BCC/Bcc field node specifically and check that 'finance@outlook.com' appears as a child/value of that node, preventing false positives when the email is placed in TO or CC.
Re-run rule validation after the 'check_' prefix fix to confirm the metric function is now correctly discovered and the validation_passed status can be updated.
